notes.title: Replace database calls for cloudflare worker agent
notes.description: It will be increasingly expensive to keep database calls as part of the auth check for inbound mail. We can replace with a static list that is updated when a user signs up

notes.title: Design: client configuration
notes.description: Define the configuration Boardy will produce and every agent reads: what Obed extracts and how, the rules Justice checks, Noti's destinations. Structured fields vs free-text instructions; versioning and approval; which version each event used; one or several workflows per client. See Planner.md, 'Design on paper'.

notes.title: Design: event lifecycle
notes.description: Event states and allowed moves (e.g. received → processing → extracted → judged → delivered), failure points, failed vs needs_review, delivery retries, what each step records for the timeline. See Planner.md, 'Design on paper'.

notes.title: Design: Rolepay payload
notes.description: The JSON Rolepay's webhook receives, drafted from a redacted payslip: which fields, several payslips per email, where event_id / verdict / per-field confidence go, the failure payload, schema versioning. See Planner.md, 'Design on paper'.

notes.title: Reject emails until client onboarding is complete
notes.description: Add a client status (onboarding → active → suspended). The Worker's recipient check rejects clients that aren't active, with a bounce message giving the reason, before any Function call, storage or LLM cost.

notes.title: Event tracking: events, event_steps, results
notes.description: Built in E5 (migration 8d3f6b1e4a27): events, event_sources, event_steps, deliveries; recorded at the start and end of every run (agents/store/events.py), duplicates skipped, billable flag, personal_data_expires_at. The ingest_id is the event_id.

notes.title: Obed: payslip extraction with structured output
notes.description: Roadmap step 1. A plain script, no framework: one payslip → JSON validated against a Pydantic model. Compare OCR vs a model that can read images. Email content is untrusted; Obed gets no outbound tools.

notes.title: Orchy: LangGraph orchestration graph
notes.description: Roadmap step 2. Wrap Obed in a LangGraph graph: state, nodes, deterministic checks, conditional edges for retry/fail. Orchy is the graph itself, not an LLM.

notes.title: Deterministic checks before Justice
notes.description: Plain-code validation: matches the schema; business rules (gross − deductions = net, plausible tax, valid dates). Free, instant, no hallucination.

notes.title: Justice: LLM-as-judge confidence and verdict
notes.description: Roadmap step 3. Runs on every result after the checks. Outputs per-field confidence, a verdict (accepted / needs_review / failed) and readable reasons. Use a different model from Obed; evaluate Justice against the labelled test set. Roughly doubles LLM cost per request.

notes.title: Noti: channel adapters, webhook first
notes.description: Webhook delivery built in E3 (agents/noti/): Standard Webhooks HMAC signing, one secret per destination (encrypted in destination_secrets), retries for 5xx/429/timeouts with exponential waits, redirects not followed, every attempt recorded. Other channels: see 'Notification channels beyond webhooks'.

notes.title: Run the graph from the ingest queue
notes.description: Built and deployed in E6 (2026-10-13): Container Apps job caj-3lay-orchy, woken by the ingest-jobs queue; agents/jobs/ingest.py; poison queue after 5 attempts. See agents/DEPLOY.md.

notes.title: Evaluation test set and tracing
notes.description: Tracing works (LangSmith, synthetic documents only; switched off in tests). Left: a test set of 10–20 documents with hand-checked gold standards (scripts/make_gold.py, evaluate.py). Plan: Boardy's onboarding produces each client's test set from their sample documents.

notes.title: Prompt injection defences
notes.description: Partly done: Obed's system rules say the inputs are data, never instructions; Obed has no tools; destinations come only from configuration. Left: documents with planted instructions in the test set, and checking how well each model resists them.

notes.title: Personal data and UK GDPR
notes.description: Payslips contain names, NI numbers, pay and tax; 3lay is a data processor. Decide LLM provider data terms and processing region (e.g. Azure AI Foundry UK South), retention of raw emails and results, and a data processing agreement with Rolepay.

notes.title: Swappable models per agent
notes.description: Done for Obed: the model comes from AGENTS:OBED_MODEL (any provider with structured output). Left: a model catalogue per agent and task type, combined with the per-region catalogue for data residency.

notes.title: Run dashboard in the frontend
notes.description: Roadmap step 6. Client view of events by event_id, a step timeline for failures, the verdict and per-field confidence, and metrics: volume, failure rate, average confidence, delivery success.

notes.title: Boardy: onboarding chat agent
notes.description: NEXT. The first agent with tools: builds a client's configuration through a conversation (add_document_type, add_rule, set_destination, try_on_samples), checked by check_configuration as it goes; tries the draft on the client's sample documents (Obed + rules) and shows the envelopes; produces the client's gold standard; saves a draft that the client approves. LangGraph interrupt, Postgres checkpointer, runs in the backend. Must ask about every configurable option rather than assume Rolepay's. First version: a terminal-driven Boardy that rebuilds Rolepay's configuration.

notes.title: Notification channels beyond webhooks
notes.description: SMS and other triggers as Noti adapters, with a message template per destination (start with deterministic templates).

notes.title: End-user profiles
notes.description: Profiles for clients' end users (e.g. Rolepay's actors), keyed by sender address (origin).

notes.title: More inbound channels
notes.description: WhatsApp, SMS and other channels besides email. A WhatsApp bot holds an ongoing conversation with end users as the client's own bot (3lay invisible; 3lay may be its own client), chained together by case_ref. Chat messages aren't events: an event is created only when the conversation hands work to the pipeline.

notes.title: Reprocessing events (runs)
notes.description: An event can be reprocessed (new schema version, better model). Each run has its own steps and result; the latest is current, earlier runs kept as history. Every run is delivered with its run number. Retries of transient errors are attempts within a run. See Planner.md step 2.

notes.title: Watchdog for stuck events
notes.description: Needed before a real client relies on the pipeline: a crash leaves an events row in 'processing'. Mark events stuck in processing too long as failed (processing_timeout, not billable) and deliver event.failed, so the client always hears about every event. Runs with the owner's database connection.

notes.title: Error code catalogue
notes.description: Stable, documented error codes for failed events and rejected items (no_documents_found, unsupported_file_type, document_unreadable, not_a_relevant_document, processing_error, processing_timeout). Part of the client contract; never renamed.

notes.title: Delivery tracking, retries and resend
notes.description: Done: delivery status per destination and attempt (deliveries table), retries within the run, client-set retry waits within 3lay's limits, failed events delivered too. Left: the resend button in the dashboard (and a resend for deliveries that gave up).

notes.title: Human review of needs_review results
notes.description: Later: let clients approve or correct needs_review results in the dashboard, then deliver the corrected result. For now needs_review is inform only.

notes.title: Configuration versions and approval
notes.description: Done (E4): client_configurations with versions, one active per client, check_configuration, events record their config_version; secrets outside the configuration. Left: the draft → approved → active approval step (comes with Boardy and the dashboard).

notes.title: Rule types as data
notes.description: A fixed set of rule types the checks understand (sum_equals, percentage_of, compare, date_within, required, allowed_values), each with on_fail: needs_review or reject. Works within a document and across documents. Boardy chooses from them; it can't write code.

notes.title: Orchy: classify attachments into document types
notes.description: Orchy's one LLM step: each attachment → one of the client's document types (by its description), or unknown → rejected item (not_a_relevant_document). Then fan out one branch per document (LangGraph fan-out / fan-in).

notes.title: Cross-document analyses
notes.description: Optional steps across all documents in a case (e.g. match an invoice to its purchase order), with their own rules and/or instructions and output schema. Rerun across the whole case when a new event joins it. Results go in the envelope's analyses list.

notes.title: Billing per event and monthly cap
notes.description: Done: events.billable follows the policy (completed and sender-caused failures billed; processing_error / processing_timeout not). Left: plans priced on events per month and documents per event, the monthly cap with a warning at 80% and bouncing at the Worker when reached.

notes.title: Edit configuration in the dashboard
notes.description: Clients can edit their configuration directly as well as through Boardy. Every edit creates a new version that goes through the same validation and needs approval.

notes.title: Intake rules: sender allowlists
notes.description: For now anyone can send to a client's address. Later: allowlists of senders or domains, or known end users only, bounced at the Worker so they're never billed.

notes.title: Cases and case matching (case_ref)
notes.description: Every event belongs to a case (case_ref in the envelope); by default a new one. Events join an existing case by configured strategies: thread (email reply headers / chat conversation), a reference in the email, a matching extracted field, or sender + time window. Analyses run across the whole case. Cases close explicitly or after inactivity (client configurable, default 7 days). Optional client-supplied case references. Rolepay doesn't use cases. Boardy asks about all of this.

notes.title: Data residency per client
notes.description: Client configuration states data_residency (none, uk, eu, us); Boardy asks about it. 3lay keeps a model catalogue per region in App Config and routes every model call to a deployment in that region (e.g. Rolepay: none; a client requiring Europe: EU-hosted models). Also needs blobs, database and traces in the region for a real guarantee. Hugging Face partners must be pinned to the region. See Planner.md step 1, Data residency.

notes.title: Obed: dates extracted in the wrong order
notes.description: Models copy printed dates digit by digit into the YYYY-MM-DD slots (05.01.2026 -> 0501-01-20), across every model tried. Tried adding <field>_as_printed before each date field (2026-10-06): copying became perfect but the model still converted wrongly 2 of 3 times, so it was reverted. Proposed fix: Obed copies dates as printed; code converts to YYYY-MM-DD (day first by default per client, unambiguous when a part > 12, ambiguous dates flagged needs_review). Dates become a 3lay building block Boardy can use.

notes.title: Delete personal data after 90 days
notes.description: Needed before a real client relies on the pipeline. A job (owner's connection, not agents_pipeline) that, for events past personal_data_expires_at, clears the envelope and sender and the sources' extraction and checks, keeping statuses, counts, timings, tokens and billable. Also decide how long raw emails in Blob Storage are kept (a lifecycle rule).

notes.title: Model fallbacks across providers
notes.description: Before a real client relies on the pipeline. Each agent pins one provider (Obed: gemma-4-31B-it:novita; Boardy: gpt-oss-120b:groq), so a provider outage stops it: on 2026-10-13 Hugging Face's circuit breaker paused DeepInfra for gpt-oss-120b. Make each model setting a fallback list (e.g. ovhcloud, then scaleway, then together) using LangChain's with_fallbacks, containing only providers that support what the agent needs (tools for Boardy, structured output for Obed; check with scripts/list_models.py --check). Record which provider served each call in the step details. Also seen 2026-10-13: groq answers 400 tool_use_failed when the model writes invalid JSON for a tool call (a large set_schema); that's worth one retry, then the next provider.

notes.title: Boardy: sample corrections become the client's gold standard
notes.description: Deferred from B4 (Seth, 2026-10-13). After try_on_samples, the client says which values are wrong (e.g. line 2's net should be 450); a record_correct_values(sample_id, corrections) tool stores the expected output per sample in the draft, saved with the configuration in B5. Those samples and values are the client's gold standard, used by B6 (evaluating Boardy) and Justice. Seen in the first real run: the payslip's PAYE and NI deductions sit in a separate section, so they were missed per line: exactly what a correction would catch.

notes.title: Boardy: cap tool rounds per turn
notes.description: In a real run (2026-10-13) groq called set_schema 23 times in one turn because the $id error message didn't say underscores weren't allowed (fixed: underscores allowed, clearer message). Nothing stops a turn looping like that, and each round costs a model call. Cap the tool rounds per turn (count them in the state; past the limit, the tools node answers 'stop and ask the client' instead of running), rather than LangGraph's recursion_limit, which would stop mid-step and leave tool calls unanswered in the saved conversation.
